sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for project totals
sections.what: Brings in the data-fetching tools, the totals type, the request helper, and the login check.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are needed to fetch and cache the totals.

sections.name: PROJECT_TOTALS_QUERY_KEY
sections.title: Shared cache label for totals
sections.what: Defines the cache label for the totals and places it under the portfolio label.
sections.why: The comment says placing it under the portfolio label means refreshing the portfolio also refreshes totals.
sections.watch_out: Renaming the portfolio label silently breaks this link, so totals would go stale.

sections.name: useProjectTotals
sections.title: Fetching project totals
sections.what: Provides the live project and industry counts to any screen that shows them. It only fetches after login and refreshes when the user returns to the window.
sections.why: Likely reason: totals can change after imports, so the app rechecks them on return.
sections.watch_out: The 30-second freshness window means a count can be out of date for up to half a minute.

sections.name: formatProjectTotals
sections.title: Writing the totals sentence
sections.what: Turns the totals into a readable sentence such as a count of projects across a count of industries, with correct singular and plural words.
sections.why: Keeps the wording the same on every screen that shows totals.
sections.watch_out: The sentence uses the browser's number formatting, so separators can differ between locales.

summary: Fetches the live project counts shown on the launcher, the Yard landing page, and industry pages.
purpose: Gives every screen one shared source for the total project count and industry count.
why: The comment says a single source avoids different screens showing different totals. Placing the key under the portfolio key means one refresh updates both.
how: Checks login state. If logged in, it asks the server for totals, keeps them for 30 seconds, and refreshes them when the user returns to the window. A formatting helper turns the numbers into a readable sentence.
inputs: The login state, the server endpoint /api/portfolio/totals, and the numbers in the totals response.
outputs: A query result holding the totals, and a formatted sentence such as a count of projects across a count of industries.
risks: Changing PROJECT_TOTALS_QUERY_KEY breaks the link with the portfolio refresh. The sentence wording is fixed in English.
debug: Check the totals endpoint in the network panel. If counts look stale after an import, confirm the portfolio cache was invalidated.
